correctness.rationale: The primitive 2-uniform four-letter substitution a->ab,b->ac,c->db,d->dc and code a,b=+, c,d=- reproduce the binary Rudin-Shapiro definition. Solving all sixteen hidden-pair stationarity equations yields eight frequency-1/8 pairs. A parity-split terminating rational recursion through length ten yields each of 32 sign-resolved complete adjacent-run frequencies and excludes either five-equal-sign factor. Independently solved recurrence gave Q=(1/64)[[2,2,2,2],[2,0,0,0],[3,0,1,0],[1,0,1,0]]. Rows normalize to p=(1/2,1/8,1/4,1/8), transition P and mutual information 1/8+3/16 log2(3); primitive substitution makes frequencies true infinite limits, not a finite-prefix extrapolation.
